## REASONING

The user asks a flux question — "true steady-state annual recharge reaching the deep water table" — aggregated across the Naches (HUC 17030002). This decomposes into two goals: (1) a mechanistic/quantitative goal — estimate deep recharge (ELM's sub-surface drainage/recharge, QDRAI/QRECHARGE / QDRAI) and how it varies with the drivers across the basin; and (2) an implied validation goal — but note recharge itself has NO in-domain observation (recharge measurements are listed as missing), so recharge cannot be validated directly. The only observations are WTD (USGS wells + Fan 2013 prior), which we can use to constrain/validate the water-table state that gates recharge, as a proxy — not as recharge validation.

Feasibility, honestly: recharge and water table are SLOW states. Per the execution limits, any such design MUST include spin-up or a WTD-informed warm start, because a cold start pins every column at ~8.8 m and reads recharge ≈ 0 while storage fills. Naches is in CONUS, so NLDAS-2 (~12 km) forcing is available and elevation-orographic precipitation IS partially resolved — good, since precipitation is the dominant recharge driver. So single-column ELM CAN produce a physically meaningful vertical recharge flux per column, warm-started from Fan (2013) WTD.

The critical caveats that make the verdict PARTIAL, not full:
- "TRUE steady-state" and "the deep water table" imply a regional, lateral-flow-equilibrated system. ELM columns are 1-D with NO lateral transport and no regional water table. ELM's recharge is vertical drainage out of the column, which is NOT the same as net recharge to a laterally-connected regional aquifer (discharge zones in valley bottoms can have net-zero or negative recharge under lateral inflow that ELM cannot represent). So we can report ELM 1-D vertical recharge, area-weighted to a basin estimate — but "true" steady-state regional recharge would need coupling/routing we don't have.
- There is no recharge observation to validate against, in-domain or analog. We validate the WTD state instead and flag recharge itself as an unvalidated model output.

Drivers: candidate_drivers = soil, forcing. Soil (SSURGO) is a real lever. Forcing varies with location/elevation via NLDAS, so an elevation-banded placement DOES sample a real precipitation gradient here (unlike a uniform-forcing case). I stratify by elevation band (proxy for the orographic precip gradient) × dominant soil texture, and area-weight for the basin aggregate.

N: recharge is soil × climate driven, so ~3 elevation/precip bands × 2–3 soil groups ≈ 12 exploratory columns, plus validation columns pinned to whatever USGS wells fall in-domain (count unknown until the well inventory is queried). I place 12 concrete exploratory columns spanning the bbox and elevation range.
